Explain the example for resize an object with scale

blocks.text: Scale multiplies an object's size on each axis. A scale of one keeps its original size.

Use a browser project with the three package installed and a module build tool. Each example creates its own canvas. Run one at a time. These library imports are not supported by this site's plain runner.

blocks.title: Resize an object with scale

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `scale.set` multiplies an object's size along x, y and z. Equal values keep the same proportions.
A perspective camera needs a field of view, aspect ratio, near distance and far distance to describe its view.
`MeshBasicMaterial` gives a visible surface without requiring lights. It is useful for a first shape example.

blocks.text: The cube becomes twice as wide and half as tall, while its depth stays unchanged.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Non-uniform scale can stretch a shape. Use equal values when you want to keep its proportions.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Set all three scale values to 1.5.
